title: ConsumerSessionOps
description: Request/result bodies for the consumer-session/* operations (spec.md §8.2). Interaction specifications, variant descriptors, endpoint descriptors and contract documents are governed by their own designs (spec.md §8.1) and are open objects here.

components.description: The project's declared components, **resolved** by the host's loader (spec.md §8.2, lifecycle-hooks spec §7.1): each entry is design 2.6's ComponentDeclaration (component-interfaces component-config.schema.json) with a 'file' source's path made absolute. The engine loads them when the session is created and fails the create — not the first interaction that needs one — when one cannot be loaded. A session's components are its own and end with it.

redaction.title: Redaction
redaction.description: What the contract records redacted beyond the members the transport declares as credentials, and which of those it records as they are (spec.md §8.2, contract-file spec §5.6, ADR 0074). Each entry is a path: a part, a slot, then member names, as a plan path is spelled without its '$.'. A path that does not parse fails the create with 'malformed-frame'.

add.description: Members to record redacted, and never to report, beyond the transport's.

keep.description: Members to record as they are, though the transport or 'add' names them: a fixed token a provider's test environment accepts. A kept value is still never reported.

AddPactInteraction.title: AddPactInteraction
AddPactInteraction.description: consumer-session/add-pact-interaction (spec.md §8.2, ADR 0066): a v1–v4 interaction as a consumer library builds it through pact_ffi, added as add-interaction adds an interaction specification.

PactSteps.title: PactSteps
PactSteps.description: A v1–v4 interaction as a consumer library builds it through pact_ffi (spec.md §8.2, ADR 0066): the calls it makes, in order, which the engine applies as pact_ffi does to an interaction that starts empty, then converts as upgrade/pact converts a pact's interaction.

specification.description: The pact specification the library would write, which decides what some calls add (with_binary_file's body rule, from V3). Default 'V4'.

PactStep.title: PactStep
PactStep.description: One pact_ffi call, named without its 'pactffi_' prefix, its arguments by name (spec.md §8.2 lists them). 'part' is 'request' or 'response'. A value the FFI takes as integration JSON in a string is the JSON value, a string being the text as given. A file the FFI would read is its name and its octets, base64-encoded.

call.description: Open vocabulary: a call the engine does not make is 'interaction-invalid', pointing at it.

handle.description: Identifies the interaction within this session; invalid after finalise.
Identifies the interaction within this session, as add-interaction's handle does.

findings.description: What converting the built interaction lost or decided (ADR 0066 decision 3), in contract-file spec §8.4's vocabulary; present when there is any.

code.description: Open vocabulary; an unknown code is displayed, never dispatched on. Codes are listed in contract-file spec §8.4.

kind.description: 'lossy', 'judgement' or 'note', as contract-file spec §8.4 means them.

path.description: RFC 6901 JSON pointer into the v4 interaction the steps built, as a pact would hold it; the empty pointer is the whole interaction.

target.description: RFC 6901 JSON pointer into the interaction specification the conversion produced, when the construct ended up somewhere.

policy.description: Per-call sampling policy override (design 2.3), for a host offering an '--exhaustive'-style switch. The resolution order is spec-defaults, session config, interaction spec, then this.

variants.description: The selection, in run order — the variants the engine chose, not the whole space (design 2.3).

report.description: How the selection was chosen: space size, strategy, coverage, exclusions (design 2.3).

VariantDescriptor.title: VariantDescriptor
VariantDescriptor.description: The protocol requires only 'id'; the rest belongs to design 2.3, which defines the id, the assignment it derives from, the display label and the origin.

endpoint.description: Open endpoint descriptor document — host/port for HTTP, broker/topic details for messaging (spike 1.5).

parts.description: An emissive interaction with no transport of its kind started in the session: the variant's message, every part of it, as a transport would carry it, for the host to hand to its test (spec.md §8.2, ADR 0067). Absent for a passive interaction, which is armed instead.

DeliveredSlotValue.title: DeliveredSlotValue
DeliveredSlotValue.description: One slot of a delivered message, wrapped as contract spec §5.3 wraps one: a slot whose type the interaction declares is its octets, encoded by that type's content component and labelled with it, and any other slot is its value as it stands.

encoded.description: How to read 'content': 'json' is the value as it stands, 'text' a string whose octets are its UTF-8 encoding, 'base64' RFC 4648 §4 octets (ADR 0006).

content-type.description: The media type the octets are, for a slot whose type the interaction declares.

ReportVariant.title: ReportVariant
ReportVariant.description: The test's verdict on one variant, once its closure has ended (spec.md §8.2, ADR 0064). It ends the variant's run: an exchange under way for it is recorded first, and the variant is disarmed.

status.description: The test's verdict. Any value but 'passed' counts as 'failed'.

reason.description: What the test failed with, as text. Recorded, and never read by the engine.

result.description: The variant's result as 'finalise' would report it now.

write.title: ContractWrite
write.description: Write the contract to a file through the engine's host (spec.md §8.2, ADR 0065), behind the 'contract-writing' capability. Nothing is written when the contract is withheld.

path.description: The file, as an absolute path; its directory is created.

mode.description: 'merge' (the default) joins the file's interactions and the session's by identity, failing with 'contract-conflict' on one recorded differently; 'overwrite' writes the session's contract whatever the file held.

contract.description: The Janus contract document (design 2.5); present iff every interaction verified successfully on its required variants and, for a host that declared 'test-verdicts', the session refused no interaction; and the host did not declare 'contract-text' or ask for the contract to be written. Persistence is the host's business.

contract-text.description: In place of 'contract', to a host that declared the 'contract-text' capability (ADR 0063): the contract's canonical bytes (contract-file spec §2.4) as text, its trailing LF included, present exactly when 'contract' would be. A host writes its UTF-8 encoding and nothing else.

written.description: In place of 'contract' and 'contract-text', when the request carried 'write' and the contract was not withheld (ADR 0065): the path the engine's host wrote it to.

refused.description: To a host that declared 'test-verdicts' (ADR 0064): every 'add-interaction' this session refused, in order. Any refusal withholds the contract.

description.description: The submitted document's 'description', when it had one.

code.description: The refusal's error code, such as 'interaction-invalid'.

status.description: In order (spec.md §8.2): 'failed' when the test was reported failed or the exchange failed; 'not-exercised' when nothing exercised the variant; 'not-reported' when the host declared 'test-verdicts' and no report arrived; otherwise 'verified'.

mismatches.description: Mismatch documents in the plan grammar's result form (design 2.4).

test.description: The test's verdict, as the latest 'report-variant' for this variant gave it (ADR 0064). Absent until one arrives.

exercised.description: false when the test was reported failed and nothing exercised the variant: the report decides 'status', and this says what 'not-exercised' would have, so a host can show it beside the test's own failure (spec.md §8.2). Absent otherwise.
